ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and release the driver-side amount; confirm the driver did not press "I'm Here" so no waiting/cancellation fee can stand.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the driver [F4], so the fee can only stand through NS-0 → NS-1/NS-2 [NS-0]. NS-1 requires (i) an arrival confirmation — the driver pressing "I'm Here" or a platform auto-confirmation. The record shows neither: driver_pressed_here_at is null and no automatic arrival was recorded, while the driver himself admits post-hoc "I forgot to press the I'm Here button" [F6][F12]. Condition (i) therefore fails and NS-1 cannot be satisfied [NS-1].

Because NS-1 fails on (i), the fee must be refunded in full [NS-2]. The trace's ✗ on (ii) and (iii) is a consequence of there being no confirmation moment to measure from (m_from_pickup_at_tap is empty [F6]); I do not need to decide those, as (i) alone settles the branch. The driver's later statement that he waited at the pickup is a claim, not an arrival confirmation, and NS-1 (i) is not satisfied by a post-trip assertion of having been present [F12][NS-1].

I have checked the whole chat and statement for any threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation: Chat #1 is a pickup identification ("At the pickup point, silver Toyota Altis"), Chat #2 is a neutral cancellation notice, and the written statement is a factual account [F9][F10][F12]. There is no hostile or abusive language aimed at the other party, so safety_concern is "none" [SAFE-1].

The record does not support the trace's extra step of a fake arrival confirmation: no confirmation of any kind is on record, so the NS-2 flag_account limb (pressing "I'm Here" while not at the pickup) is not triggered [F6][F1][NS-2]. Both briefs request no_action, but their requested outcome contradicts NS-2, which mandates full refund once NS-1 (i)–(iii) fails [NS-2]. Amount: the cancellation fee on record is $6.61 [F4][F7], refundable in full = $6.61 [NS-2].
